## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column needs fixing before merge because it holds the start time of processes that are still running. Its catalog entry also misstates what NULL means, as traced against the `process_events` event types.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — finished_at holds the start time of running processes — For process 20, whose latest event is `'started'`, `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` fills `finished_at` with the start time `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`. The column describes a process that is still running. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `'created'`, `'started'` and `'cleared'`, so no event marks a finish. — Consumers will read every running process as already finished, at its start time. — Fix: Rename the column to `started_at` and update `models/schema.yml:9-11` to match, or add a finish event type to `sources/process_events.sql:4` and select on that.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the NULL meaning in the finished_at description — For process 30, which was started and then cleared, the model returns NULL because its latest event is `'cleared'`. The description says "NULL means the process has never been started", which is false for that process. Line 14 confirms that only the latest event contributes to the row. — Anyone filtering on `finished_at is null` to find processes that never started will also get processes that started and were later cleared.
